messages:
leo (Acme): Hey team — seeing a pretty bad stream failure in prod. Client gets a partial output then SSE disconnect, client reconnects and we sometimes see a duplicate final completion (same text twice) and other times it resumes mid-sentence. Happening ~5% of streams for a single endpoint since 06:00 UTC.

maria (CSE): Sorry you're hitting that, leo. Can you share a full repro (curl/JS snippet) + the request id from the first attempt? Also is this via Redwood hosted API or Dedicated?

leo (Acme): Hosted. Repro is below — simple EventSource reconnect on network loss. We include a session token as discussed.

```js
const es = new EventSource('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=xlarge', { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer sk-...' } });
es.onmessage = e => console.log('msg', e.data);
es.onerror = () => { es.close(); setTimeout(() => reconnect(), 300); }
function reconnect() { // resend resumeToken header if we have one
  const headers = { Authorization: 'Bearer sk-...', 'X-Resume-Token': resumeToken || '' };
  const es2 = new EventSource('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=xlarge', { headers });
}
```

Latest root request id: req_01F8X2ABCD (first attempt at 06:12:34 UTC). I can share full client logs privately.

ankur (Support): Thanks. I pulled logs for req_01F8X2ABCD. Server shows initial stream started (alloc id g-77), then client reconnect at +1.8s with X-Resume-Token: rt_7z, we accepted the resume, but there are two generation events created: gen-345 (first) and gen-346 (resume). gen-346 re-emitted some tokens from gen-345 and also produced a duplicate final chunk.

sam (Infra SRE): Noted. I'm seeing a short window where resume tokens are valid but the session token associated with a request rotates (we have a refresh happening at 1s TTL in this customer's tenant due to legacy config). If the resume request uses a freshly minted session token, the runtime may create a new generation record instead of attaching to the existing one. That could explain duplicates.

leo (Acme): So is the dup coming from the server treating resumed session as new? We're billed twice for the duplicated tokens — customer upset.

maria (CSE): Short term: we can credit the duplicate tokens for the customer. Medium term we need a fix. Need eng help to confirm exact race.

julie (eng-runtime): Quick context from runtime side: resume flow uses two checks — resume token validity and mapping to open generation id. If the session auth changes between initial and reconnect we currently revalidate and will spawn a new generation if mapping doesn't match 1:1. That was intentional for strict auth, but it causes duplicate emission if the new gen replays cached prefix.

julie (eng-runtime): Repro steps I used locally: 1) start stream with resume token rt_A; 2) force auth rotate (simulate new session id); 3) reconnect with same rt_A but different session; 4) runtime created gen-A and gen-B where gen-B pulled cached tokens but also re-generated tail. Logs: 

```
[2025-11-12T06:12:34Z] stream-start req=req_01F8X2ABCD gen=345 resume=rt_7z
[2025-11-12T06:12:36Z] auth-rotate tenant=acme old_sid=sid_1 new_sid=sid_2
[2025-11-12T06:12:36Z] reconnect req=req_01F8X2ABCD resume=rt_7z provided_sid=sid_2 -> mapped_sid=sid_1 mismatch -> spawn gen=346
[2025-11-12T06:12:36Z] gen=346 re-emitted prefix tok(0..42) then generated tok(43..end)
```

julie (eng-runtime): The subtlety is that our prefix cache is keyed only by resume token, not session id, so gen-346 replays prefix then proceeds to produce new continuation. That yields duplicate prefix in client stream plus two completions if both gens finish.

ankur (Support): That's the dup root cause — thanks. Possible mitigations?

julie (eng-runtime): Options: 
- Quick mitigation: treat resume token + session id as atomic pair during resume lookup. If session id mismatches, do NOT spawn a new gen; instead reject the resume and instruct client to refetch full non-resume request (loses resume but avoids duplicate).
- Better: allow resume across session rotation by mapping resume token to a stable generation id AND attach a short-lived session binding (grace period ~5s) so small rotates won't force new gen.
- Long term: generate idempotency keys derived from prompt hash + initial-gen-seq so we can dedupe on writes to the generation table and billing meter.

sam (Infra SRE): We can flip a config flag to extend resume grace to 5s in production for this tenant. That would reduce likelihood of duplicates while eng ships a proper fix.

maria (CSE): Leo, can we apply the 5s grace and issue a credit now?

leo (Acme): Yes please — credits would help while you fix. Also customers are using our library which auto-reconnects on network blips; might be worth warning in docs.

julie (eng-runtime): Action items I propose: 
- sam: rollback to increase resume grace window to 5s for hosted tenants (ops change) — ETA 2 hours.
- julie: patch runtime resume lookup to require resume token + session binding or fall back to rejecting resume (PR+tests) — ETA 3 days.
- julie: add dedupe-by-idempotency-key in generation creation to prevent billing duplicates — design doc in 1 day.
- ankur/maria: apply customer credits and notify leo.

ankur (Support): I'll create a billing ticket and attach sample logs. maria can you confirm wording for the credit message?

maria (CSE): Yes. I'll handle comms and ask for client logs to harden repro.

leo (Acme): Thanks all. One more ask: our client library can send both resume token + prior request id in header. If you need additional fields to safely resume, tell us and we'll upgrade.

julie (eng-runtime): That's helpful — please include previous gen id (if you persist it) and a resume-seq number on reconnects. We'll make resume semantics explicit in docs.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: ops/extend-resume-grace -> prod at 08:30 UTC (2h).

sam (Infra SRE): ops change done — grace window extended to 5s for hosted. Monitoring on duplicated-completions metric enabled (alert threshold 0.5% for any tenant).

maria (CSE): Leo, we've issued a credit covering estimated duplicate tokens and opened a follow-up to track engineering fix. Please DM client logs to me.

leo (Acme): Good work. Will DM logs now and keep monitoring. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :rocket:
